extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners and media scholars (press officers in corporations, NGOs, unions, political comms; media-relations strategists)
extracted.subtask_description: Sector-specific criteria for designing press releases to maximize media pickup in Britain; emphasizes how corporate, financial, pressure-group, trade-union and political domains require different package elements (briefings, exclusives, coalitions, reframing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-briefed City editor relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoed pre-briefings to FT/WSJ City editors convert at higher rates than open wire blasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target and pre-brief specific City editors under embargo rather than relying on broad wire distribution for financial/City stories; cultivate and use embargoed relationships to increase pickup probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyst-meeting alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases timed to align with the analyst meeting cycle land into existing routine channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule release timing to coincide with analyst cycles and routine financial-calendar events so the material fits editors' and analysts' rhythms and is more likely to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEO/CFO quotability discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes that satisfy disclosure rules (no forward-looking guidance ad lib) and supply a usable headline phrase score higher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft executive quotes to be legally compliant, non-speculative, and to contain concise, quotable headline phrases; avoid ad-lib forward guidance that breaks disclosure norms or reduces usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade-press integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry-specific framing (sector context, peer comparison) earns trade-press pickup that subsequently feeds national pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sector context, peer benchmarking and language tailored to trade media so trade coverage can seed broader national coverage; think of trade-press as a conduit to general outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-quote piggyback
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource-poor groups achieve pickup by attaching a counter-quote to a corporate or government release that day. Releases issued in isolation rarely break through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time releases to coincide with major corporate/government announcements and provide an immediate counter-quote or reaction to piggyback on the dominant story; avoid standalone releases with no hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource-poor groups that supply pre-packaged investigation material (documents, FOI returns, original data) earn pickup proportional to the news value of the investigation, not their PR resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide original, verifiable materials (documents, FOI returns, datasets) packaged for journalists; news value drives pickup even for low-resource issuers—focus on provable, novel evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story-package readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-supplied case studies (named affected individuals, story arc, willing-to-be-quoted families) compensate for lack of corporate brand recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include human case studies with named, quote-ready sources and a clear narrative arc to make stories tangible and usable for reporters who may otherwise ignore unknown issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coalition signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup increases when a resource-poor group can demonstrate a coalition (multiple named groups, joint signatories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signal breadth and credibility by coordinating joint statements, multiple named endorsers or coalition membership to suggest the issue has wider support and thus is more newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer-impact reframing
rubrics_metrics.description: Union releases reach lay press only when reframed as consumer-impact rather than labor-relations stories. The release author must do this reframing or the editor will not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reframe industrial/labor issues in terms of consumer or public impact (costs, service disruption, household effects) to gain general-interest media attention; do the reframing within the release copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of insider-jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: Union jargon (negotiating positions, pay-band terminology) is stripped or rejected; releases must be written for a general newsroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in plain English, avoiding sector-specific jargon and technical terms; translate negotiation language into everyday consequences and clear explanations for non-specialist journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobby-correspondent fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Political releases targeted at the parliamentary lobby work through prior trust relationships; outsider distribution mechanisms do not penetrate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established lobby-correspondent relationships and tailored targeting for parliamentary journalism; broad outsider distributions are unlikely to break into the lobby-driven political beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-the-record + on-the-record pair
rubrics_metrics.description: Sophisticated political releases pair an on-the-record release with an off-the-record briefing that primes the angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine a formal on-the-record release with complementary off-the-record briefings to frame an angle, provide context, or prime journalists—use discretion and trust relationships to manage the pair effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource-asymmetry awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: A release should be calibrated to the issuer's position in the source-journalist network — a small NGO release should not pretend to corporate scale, and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess your organisation's resource and network position and choose tactics appropriate to that scale (e.g., piggyback, coalition, exclusive, or targeted pre-briefing) rather than imitating strategies reserved for well-resourced actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-run trust accumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup is partly a function of the issuer's track record on the receiving journalist's beat — a release benefits from years of accurate prior dealings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in consistent, accurate interactions with journalists over time; credibility and a history of useful material increase the chance that future releases will be picked up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector newsroom dependence-and-trust regime
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sector operates in a different newsroom dependence-and-trust regime which shapes how releases are received and which tactics work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map the target sector's newsroom dependence (who editors rely on for info) and trust dynamics before deciding whether to use embargoes, exclusives, off-the-record briefings, piggybacking or trade-press routes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-differentiated release strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup is strongly sector-dependent and resource-asymmetric — a single one-size release strategy under-performs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate release programs by sector and customize the package (briefing, exclusive, counter-quote, coalition signal) to the news access regime relevant to each sector rather than adopting a universal approach.
